original_question: What produces gamma-ray-burst afterglow emission: how many distinct outflow components contribute at a given stage of the afterglow evolution, and what are the relative contributions of synchrotron emission and inverse-Compton emission in each observed spectral regime?
target_in_paper: "The origin of the afterglow emission also remains a puzzle. In particular, the number of distinct outflow components observed at any given phase of the afterglow evolution and the relative contributions of the synchrotron and i.c. processes at any given spectral regime are still open questions."
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies that the paper raises an open question about (1) the number of distinct outflow components contributing to GRB afterglow emission at different phases of its evolution, and (2) the relative contributions of synchrotron and inverse-Compton emission across spectral regimes.
missing_details:
Definition of “distinct outflow components” (e.g.
forward shock vs reverse shock vs additional emission regions)

Specification of afterglow phases or timescales (e.g.
early afterglow t≲1 day vs late afterglow t≳1 day)

Clarification of the spectral regimes or energy bands (e.g.
<10^2 MeV vs >10^2 MeV)
Explanation that “i.c. processes” refers to inverse-Compton scattering

Context of observational constraints (e.g.
Fermi detection of high-energy photons)
refined_question: In the context of gamma-ray-burst afterglows, at a specified post-burst time, (1) how many distinct relativistic outflow components (for example, the forward shock propagating into the ambient medium, the reverse shock driven into the ejecta, or other localized emission regions) contribute to the observed multiwavelength emission, and (2) what are the quantitative contributions of the synchrotron and inverse-Compton processes to the flux in different energy bands (for instance, below and above 10^2 MeV) during both the early (t≲1 day) and late (t≳1 day) phases of the afterglow evolution?
justification: The refined question directly quotes and expands upon the open problem stated in Section 4.3, "Uncertainties involving the emission mechanism," by defining the terms 'distinct outflow components' and 'spectral regimes,' specifying relevant timescales (early vs late afterglow), and clarifying 'i.c.' as inverse-Compton. This makes the question fully self-contained and faithful to the paper's original wording and intent.
